name: In-play two-sided sports quoting (RN1 model)
mechanism: Rest bids on BOTH outcomes of every two-outcome sports market from kickoff to final whistle, one tick wide (the two bids sum to 0.99), 2-3 levels, fixed share size per league, re-quote within seconds, never sell: pairs redeem for $1 at resolution, merge only when cash runs short. Edge is the ~1.5 cent toll per pair paid by impatient in-game buyers, plus maker rebates and a refund of part of its own taker fees. Unpaired leftovers are the cost.
time_gap: None in the maker's favour; the maker is the slow side. Fast takers with fresher scores/odds pick it off (seconds in-game, minutes to hours pre-game).
claimed_results: 10 Aug-10 Nov 2026: 911,860 fills, 222.5M spent, +1.6M from fills (0.71% of spend) plus 935K of daily payments = 2.53M; pairs +2.1M, leftovers -486K; in-game quoting +1.13M, pre-game quoting -283K; lost on 39 of 92 days, worst drawdown 323K; capital 1.2-2.7M.
evidence: wallet_check RN1 (0x2005d16a...75ea), re-run 2026-11-27: shown P/L 15,090,230; fees charged 5,343,676, refunded 3,852,784 (paid 1.49M); rebates+rewards 2,302,007 (taker 620K / maker 1.31M / rewards 375K); kept 15,901,347 = 2.13% of $747M volume; rebates/rewards 14% of kept all-time. Monthly gross / rebates / NET kept / net without rebates: Jul 1.72M / 415K / 1.83M / 1.41M; Aug 1.31M / 288K / 1.35M / 1.06M; Sep 561K / 361K / 628K / 266K; Oct 918K / 267K / 1.03M / 758K; Nov (to the 27th) 217K / 212K / 329K / 117K. Gross as % of volume: Jul 1.68, Aug 1.93, Sep 0.65, Oct 1.38, Nov 0.42. Rebates were 58% of net in Sep and 64% in Nov. Maker tier 4 (15%), 30-day maker weighted volume 19.1M; taker tier Platinum (25% under the 20-Nov table). The tool's Aug-Nov rows are consistent with the article's 2.53M for 92 days.
requirements: About $2M working capital turning over every few hours, coverage of ~1,000 live markets a day, sub-10-second re-quoting, and at least $10M of 30-day maker weighted volume for the 15% maker rebate (docs; RN1 itself runs at 19.1M). A new account gets no rebate and no fee refund.
fee_sensitivity: Maker fills pay no fee. Its own takes pay the sports rate 0.05 (1.25 c at 0.50). Without payments the fills alone earned 0.71% of spend; 37% of the quarter's total came from payments a small account will not receive. The 'half of own taker fees back' was the Aug-Nov regime (tool: 620K taker rebate against 1.36M charged since May); at RN1's current taker tier the table gives 25%.
testability: Whole-market tape (trades?condition=) for a sample of live matches gives maker-side P&L per price band and the share lost to the busiest takers; a simulated one-tick quote cannot be validated without book history (no cancels on chain), so only an upper bound is testable.
red_flags: Margin is falling (net without rebates 117K in November on $51M volume). 50 informed takers take back a third of maker profit. Pre-game quoting loses. ITF tennis is the worst series. Not a small-capital strategy: nothing here is reachable with a few hundred euros and no rebate tier.
verification: CONFIRMED. Both articles re-downloaded; every headline number (fills, spend, 0.71%, 935K, pair and leftover P&L, the four job rows, 42,885 wallets, top-50 takers -504K, ITF -331K, 39 of 92 losing days, 323K drawdown) is in the text, and the wallet tool agrees in order of magnitude. Corrected: the tier-4 threshold is $10M, not 19M.

name: Pre-match de-vigged-odds bidding with hedge in thin esports books (polymm / b00k13)
mechanism: Scrape sportsbook odds, remove the margin to get a fair probability, post a limit bid one cent above best bid wherever fair minus bid is at least 7 points, in pre-match esports markets with 20-30 cent spreads. When one side fills, bid the other so both sides cost at most 0.93; unhedged fills remain directional. Edge is a wide spread nobody else is quoting.
time_gap: Sportsbook lines move on roster/news before thin Polymarket books: minutes. It only helps if your reference is fresher than the other bots'; with 10-30 minute old odds the gap works against you.
claimed_results: Jan-Mar 2026: 3,858 bets, $95.8K volume, +$4,973 from a ~$1K start; locked arbs +$8.3K, forced directional -$3.2K. Fill rate fell 37% (Jan) -> 15% -> 5% -> 1% (Apr). Other sports net -$509. A later note says the Rust rewrite made $650 in a month (July).
evidence: wallet_check b00k13 (0x1c5575dc...84ce), re-run 2026-11-27: shown 6,293; fees charged 357, refunded 71; rebates+rewards 50 (1% of kept); kept 6,058 = 4.2% of $144K volume. Monthly NET kept: Jan 2,295; Feb 2,086; Mar 466; Apr 115; May 0; Jun 17; Jul 617; Aug -106; Sep 285; Oct 192; Nov 91 (to the 27th), on $2.7-4.7K monthly volume since September. Jan-Apr gross 4,961 matches the claimed 4,973.
requirements: $300-1,000, one VPS, an odds source refreshed far faster than 5 minutes (he pays ~$3/day for 5-minute odds from 9 API sources), team-name matching between venues, fast cancel on line moves.
fee_sensitivity: All entries are maker bids: no fee. The esports/sports taker rate 0.05 only matters if the hedge is taken. The edge did not die from fees but from faster bots and stale odds.
testability: His analytics scripts run on any public wallet (code not run here). Forward test: poll gamma for esports markets with spread above 10 cents and volume, log the book and The Odds API / Pinnacle lines every minute, count how often a 7-point bid would have been hit before versus after a line move.
red_flags: Author himself says a clone 'will mostly donate to faster bots'. Income is now under $300 a month. AI-written code shipped three mapping bugs that bet the wrong team. All published numbers are from before the window (Jan-Jul 2026); no post on kacho.io after 2026-08-13.
verification: CONFIRMED. Three posts re-read: 3,858 bets, $95,830, +$4,973, +$8.3K / -$3,184 split, 2,555-match line-move table, fill-rate decay, -$509, $3/day odds and the 'donate to faster bots' line are all there; the wallet reproduces the totals. Credibility 5 is for the truth of the account, not for the edge, which is nearly gone.

name: Pre-game stale-quote taking on sportsbook line moves and team news
mechanism: Watch a sharp reference (sportsbook lines, lineups) for pre-match sports and esports; when the line jumps, take the resting Polymarket bids/asks that have not moved, hold to resolution or sell after the book catches up. This is the other side of the two verified makers' losses.
time_gap: Sportsbook line or team-sheet news arrives minutes (sometimes tens of minutes) before resting Polymarket quotes are pulled.
claimed_results: No one claims this strategy by name. Indirect: RN1's own pre-game takes earned +7.36% after fees (+243K), all of the profit inside the last hour before start; RN1's pre-game resting bids lost 283K in 92 days (227K from fills an hour or more before start); Kacho's 7-point bids turned negative after line moves.
evidence: Not tested by anyone in the lab. Supporting measurement from Kacho: lines moved 5+ points before going live in about a third of 2,555 esports matches (CoD 60%, LoL 49%, Dota 2 37%, CS2 31%, Valorant 12%), sampled every 7-8 minutes, 6-20 Mar 2026. RN1 wallet figures as in the first candidate.
requirements: Live odds feed (Pinnacle or The Odds API paid tier), name matching, taker execution within seconds to a minute; small capital is enough because the stale size is small.
fee_sensitivity: Sports/esports taker rate 0.05: at most 1.25 c per share at 0.50. A 5-point line move leaves about 3.75 c after the fee at even odds; a 2-point move leaves under 1 c before spread and does not survive.
testability: Take RN1's pre-game maker fills from the public tape (trades?user=RN1&taker_only=false minus the taker feed), mark each to the price 30 minutes later and at resolution, and group by the taker wallet: that shows who collects the 283K and how fast. Forward: poll odds and CLOB books by REST each minute for a week.
red_flags: Inferred from the victims' accounts, not from a winner's. The BlockJuice author calls the team-sheet explanation 'my guess, still a guess'. The stale size on offer may be tiny. RN1 itself is a pre-game taker and may be the one collecting it. Kacho's line-move data is March 2026.
verification: PARTIAL. The supporting numbers are in the sources (-283K, 227K of it an hour or more before start, +7.36% / +243K, the line-move table). The figure '4,374 fills over 1,984 markets' was not found in the text of either article. The strategy itself is the researcher's inference; no source describes or claims it.

name: In-play score-feed latency taking
mechanism: Subscribe to a fast score/event feed, and when a goal, break of serve or map win lands, hit the resting quotes on Polymarket before makers re-quote; hold or sell into the stream-watching crowd.
time_gap: Official data feeds are claimed to lead TV/streams by 45-60 s and public APIs by 3-15 s; makers like RN1 re-quote within seconds (filled orders were a median 11.8 s old), so the usable gap is seconds.

The earlier note 'about 58K down in Jan-Apr' ignored the refunds and is withdrawn. The promoter does not lose, and does not show the edge he describes.

fee_sensitivity: Sports taker rate 0.05; in-game prices move 10-50 points on a goal, so the fee is small relative to a real event, but RN1's measured taker edge was only 1.36% after a fee that averaged 1.63% of what it paid.

The only source that names the strategy and a wallet is an advert, and that wallet keeps 0.12% of volume before rebates. Free feeds (ESPN ~10 s) are slower than the makers. Lowered from 3 to 2 for these reasons.

name: Breaking-news reaction on headline markets
mechanism: Monitor primary sources (press wires, company releases, official accounts) for an event that settles an open market, and buy the winning side while the book is still repricing; hold to resolution.
time_gap: Measured on one event in two markets: the book moved in the same minute as the stock (first aggressive prints 13:55:53 UTC), the first three wallets took everything under 0.30 within about 10 seconds, and the price passed 0.90 after 66-74 seconds. A reader 20-70 s behind bought at 0.50-0.85. A public hint 10 hours earlier (Trump's post) moved the price only from 0.08 to 0.11.

The article's release time (08:30 EST) is wrong by 25 minutes per the stock tape, so its timeline cannot be used as a trigger clock. mechanism: Mirror the buys of wallets with large all-time profit (or a high skill score) shortly after their fills appear.
time_gap: Negative: the follower is hundreds of milliseconds to minutes behind the leader, and the book moves on the leader's fill.

name: Near-certain 'bond' buying and settlement-lag discount
mechanism: Two variants that should be kept apart: (1) buy the side of an event that is already decided but not yet resolved, at 0.95-0.99, and wait for resolution; (2) buy the 'almost surely' side of an event that is still open (NO at 0.90-0.96 on unlikely things) and collect the discount. The return is the discount.
time_gap: Variant 1: event known, market unresolved: hours (UMA window) to months (the Ethiopia market stayed open 123 days after the election). Variant 2 has no time gap; it is selling insurance.

sources.author: Luke Garrison (summarising Reddit u/marvmarv2693)
sources.kind: news summary of a Reddit thread

claimed_results: Reddit backtest: settlement-lag discounts listed among ten ideas that failed (fee model unknown). Paper: the discount is a maturity-dependent price of locked capital; adjusting for it removes 48-88% of the apparent mispricing.
evidence: A named wallet found in the Huang tape: Tigerofthehood (0x9c261746...74bc), 267 markets, 19,689 fills, $38.9M volume, kept 270,051 = 0.69% of volume, rebates+rewards 4% of kept. Monthly NET kept: Dec-25 11,101; Jan 23,464; Feb -26,930; Mar 54,193; Apr 9,399; May 64,828; Jun 115,281; Jul -44,006; Aug 33,110; Sep 42,384; Oct 39,368; Nov -52,140. It bought NO on 'Huang rejoins' at 0.90 (15,620 shares, Dec-31 market) and 0.958 (35,000 shares, Nov-30 market) as a taker on 16-17 November and dumped 68,991 and 66,465 NO at 0.003-0.032 at 13:57 on the 23rd: about -46K on the visible part, about -120K if the rest of the position cost the same. Lab's earlier tape: buying at 0.90-1.00 in BTC 5m was the only positive taker bucket (+0.41 c per share after fees, not significant).
requirements: Capital that can sit locked; careful reading of resolution rules; diversification across many small positions. At 0.69% of volume the verified wallet needed $39M of turnover to keep $270K; a few hundred euros earns cents.
fee_sensitivity: Fee at p=0.97 is 0.15 c at rate 0.05 and 0.03 c at 0.01; zero on geopolitics. The fee is not the problem; the tail (a surprise, a dispute, a rule reading) and the lock-up are.
testability: data-api resolutions + prices-history (30-minute buckets kept 90 days): for markets that traded above 0.95 before resolution, compute realised return, days locked, and the frequency of reversals by category, separately for 'already decided' and 'still open'. Deconstruct Tigerofthehood's 267 markets to see which variant it runs and what the three losing months were.
red_flags: One surprise wiped out roughly five average months of the verified bond wallet. Search summaries (not opened) report over 1,150 UMA disputes in 2026 and a 0.99 market overturned by vote. Volume in dead markets is largely wash trading per Wired ($284M of $285M in the Ethiopia market), so displayed liquidity is not real. The Reddit result is second-hand.
verification: CONFIRMED for the sources: the arXiv abstract (48-88%), Wired (123 days, $284M between paired accounts, 38,000 loops, over 98% with no gain or loss, 99.6% flagged in the Romania market) and the Action Network line on settlement-lag discounts are as quoted. New wallet evidence added by this pass.

name: Own pricing model in new or niche markets, taking badly priced resting orders
mechanism: Pick market types the big firms do not model (newly invented formats, low-liquidity niches), spend weeks building a better way to price them, and take resting liquidity that sits at poor prices.
time_gap: None in the latency sense; the gap is in modelling effort.
claimed_results: qoez: 'you can easily come in and price it with a large edge'; says much of his money probably comes from SIG's own quotes. PredictPnL: the top 20 by skill have 1,962-17,960 closed trades, median all-time profit $469K, median result 0.7% of volume.
evidence: None; the commenter gives no account.
requirements: Domain model per market family, patience, small capital is fine because the stale size is small.
fee_sensitivity: Mentions, culture, economics, weather are at 0.01 (0.25 c at 0.50): the cheapest categories for a taker.
testability: Category leaderboards (data-api leaderboard?category=mentions|culture|weather) to find wallets with thousands of trades and low rebate share, then deconstruct entries.
red_flags: Anonymous, no numbers, no wallet. The PredictPnL figures describe skilled wallets in general, not this approach.
verification: CONFIRMED that the comment and the article say this; the claim itself is unverifiable.

name: Polymarket-Kalshi cross-venue arbitrage and hedged quoting
mechanism: Match the same event on two venues, buy YES on one and NO on the other when the sum is under $1 after fees, or quote on one venue and hedge fills on the other.
time_gap: One venue reprices before the other: seconds.

sources.author: Luke Garrison (summarising Reddit comments)
sources.kind: news summary of a Reddit thread

claimed_results: peikail: $3-4K a day net for two weeks on Kalshi + Polymarket US, no losing day, record 'under NDA'. Reddit commenter: 233 screens a day with zero executions under strict thresholds. NBA paper: 7 executable single-market arbs in 173 games (median life 3.6 s), 290 combinatorial episodes.
evidence: None measured.
requirements: Accounts and capital on both venues. The one profit claim is on Kalshi and Polymarket US, which is a separate US venue from the Polymarket this lab studies; access for a Serbian resident not checked. Capital split and idle, automated matching of contract terms.
fee_sensitivity: Two taker fees: vendors put break-even near 3.5-4 cents per pair at even odds (search summary, not opened).
testability: Kalshi public market data and the Polymarket CLOB are both reachable here by REST: poll matched pairs and count seconds where the cross sum after both fees is under 1 and the size available.
red_flags: The only profit claim is two weeks long, unverifiable, from a job-seeker, and on a different venue. Settlement wording differs between venues. The paper and the Reddit commenter both point to near-zero executable size.
verification: CONFIRMED that the four sources say what is quoted (HN post, Show HN, Action Network line, arXiv abstract). No independent check of any result.

name: Fade longshots / base-rate NO
mechanism: Systematically sell (or avoid) cheap YES contracts on 'will X happen by date' markets, on the belief that longshots are overpriced and most such markets resolve NO.
time_gap: none

The source is a paid data product; its trading rules and sizing are not published.

name: Liquidity-reward farming (resting two-sided quotes near the midpoint)
mechanism: Keep two-sided limit orders close to the midpoint in markets with a daily reward pool. Score per order is ((v - s)/v)^2 times a market multiplier, where v is the market's maximum spread and s the distance from the midpoint; the two-sided score is the smaller of the two sides; one-sided quotes are divided by 3 and score zero when the midpoint is outside 0.10-0.90. Paid daily pro rata per market, with a $1 minimum that is not carried forward.
time_gap: none (the risk is the reverse: being filled at a stale price when news lands)
market_categories: any market with a reward pool

mechanism: Buy an outcome that is informally decided but not formally resolved at 0.93-0.99 and hold to the $1 payout. Sellers are holders who want their capital back before settlement.

claimed_results: Leo: entry at 0.97 or higher, 22 trades, 9-0, +$5.09; entry at 0.9975 or higher, 20 trades, 13-0, -$2.32 ('taker fee 2% kills you'). Guide example: Warsh nomination shares settled around 0.95 between the announcement and the formal submission.
evidence: Guide re-read: the 0.93-0.99 range, the Warsh example and '19 wins at 0.95, roughly 32 at 0.97' are there (the page dates the Warsh story to 'early 2025' and I did not find 'a couple of months'). Leo's two results re-read and correct. No wallet named. Fee arithmetic checked: at 0.97 a 0.05-rate market charges 0.146 cents per share against 3 cents gross and a 0.01-rate market 0.03 cents, so Leo's fee result does not carry over. CORRECTION on holding rewards: eligibility is the gamma flag `holdingRewardsEnabled`, true on 171 of the 1,000 most traded markets (99 zero-fee markets, 42 elections, 19 long-dated crypto price markets, 4 tech) and false on every sports, weather and tweet-count market sampled. The 3.25-4% a year therefore helps only on those long-dated markets, not on short bonds. The lab's BTC 5m tape showed buying at 0.90-1.00 as the only positive taker bucket (+0.41 cents per share, not significant).
requirements: Capital that can sit locked; reading resolution rules carefully; no speed needed for the slow version.
fee_sensitivity: Fee is close to zero near $1 under rate*p*(1-p). The edge is decided by the tail loss (one failure at 0.97 erases about 32 wins) and by lock-up time, not by fees. Note that several 0.01 categories were charged 0.04-0.05 until Nov 20, so history before that date carries a higher fee.
testability: Data API resolutions and tokens plus prices-history: for every market that traded at 0.95-0.99 inside its last days, compute the realised win rate against price, by category and by time to resolution, with fills only at prices that printed. Split by the holding-reward flag.
red_flags: Disputed and reversed resolutions (more than 1,150 disputed markets in the first five months of 2026 according to a search snippet); a perfect win rate over 20-odd trades says nothing about the tail; no source shows a track record.
verification: CONFIRMED. The mechanism and the numbers are in the guide and in Leo's post; the holding-reward statement is narrowed to flagged markets.

name: BTC 5-minute and 15-minute up/down: latency and momentum taking
mechanism: Follow the exchange price: after a Binance move take the stale side of the book, or late in the window take the direction of a steady, volume-confirmed spot trend into the averaging period; skip when the contract is already near 0.05 or 0.95.
time_gap: Exchange price to Polymarket book: under a second to about 2 s.
claimed_results: Leo: latency take suffered 75.9 basis points of adverse selection and lost $6.34 before he stopped; momentum taker, 294 live trades, win rate fell from 81% to 63%, payoff ratio 0.34, net $39. Casatrick: '[380 trades], hit rate [54.2%], edge [1.8%]'. Telonex: 36.8% of 46,945 wallets profitable in a week before fees; takers win 53% of fills and lose overall. Repeated promotional claims of '$313 into $414,000' and '98% win rate' with no wallet.
evidence: Leo's figures and Telonex's figures re-read and correct. Casatrick's page re-read: the results are printed in square brackets ('[Aug 7-21, 2026] - sample size [380 trades], hit rate [54.2%]') and the writing prompts ('Anything that surprised you: ...') are left in the text, so they are template placeholders, not measurements. Leo's and Telonex's numbers agree with the lab's own findings (takers lose 2.67% of turnover after fees). No full wallet is named by these sources.
requirements: Sub-second feed and execution near the London matching servers; high rebate tier to offset the fee.
fee_sensitivity: BTC 5m and 15m rate is 0.05 (1.25 cents per share at 0.50); other crypto 0.01. For a new account with no rebate the measured gross edge does not cover it.
testability: Already tested by the lab on the tape; the remaining variant is the late-window trend rule on post-Nov-20 data.
red_flags: The most heavily advertised idea on dev.to and Substack; the honest first-person reports are all losses; stale quotes are described as bait; the one page with 'results' never filled them in.
verification: CONFIRMED. Three sources re-opened; the losses are as quoted and the Casatrick figures are placeholders as the researcher said.

name: News to LLM to order pipeline
mechanism: Monitor headlines (wire reposts on X, Truth Social, primary sources), have a model judge the effect on a specific market, and take the stale price.
time_gap: Headline to repricing: milliseconds to seconds on major scheduled or headline events; the claimed residual is slower 'interpretation' cases where the rules are nuanced (minutes).
claimed_results: Leo, two iterations: 'By the time your order lands on the CLOB, market's already priced it in.' Hiberius: 13,860 signals, 0 fills; model latency 2-11 s against a window under 1 s. Casatrick repeats an unverified '$115,000 in a single week' for an agent framework.
evidence: Leo's sentence, Hiberius's funnel figures and the guide's 'within milliseconds' and 'interpretation' passages re-read and correct. No wallet named anywhere. The guide's 'milliseconds' is rhetoric: the lab's own measurements in NOTES.md put economic releases at 2-20 s of stale prices and headline events at 3-5 s to the first large buy, about 70 s to 95 cents. That is still shorter than the 2-11 s model latency plus order placement for the first move, but not for the tail of the move.
requirements: Fast news source, model inference under a second or a rules engine, pre-mapped markets and resolution criteria.
fee_sensitivity: Geopolitics 0, other politics and economics 0.01, elections and finance 0.05. Fees are minor against a real repricing; the problem is arriving first.
testability: For a list of timestamped announcements, pull the tape and 1-minute prices and measure the time from the public timestamp to the first fill beyond the old price, by category and market size.
red_flags: Both first-person attempts failed on speed; the positive claims are hearsay; the one supportive page is an affiliate guide without numbers.
verification: CONFIRMED. The three sources say what is quoted. No positive result exists in them.

mechanism: Fade favourites or back longshots according to historical calibration gaps, or trade order-book imbalance and wide-spread reversal signals, or train a model on price history and take when it disagrees with the price.
time_gap: none
claimed_results: The Data Scientist: equal-stake fade-favourite +25.0% and back-longshot +20.6% collapse to -50.7% and -25.5% when weighted by pre-entry liquidity; the favourite gap at 0.90-0.95 is -12.3 points by count and +6.3 points by dollar volume; LightGBM Brier 0.07784 against the market price's 0.07710 on 228,809 holdout observations; taker signal families -14.6% to -53.4% out of sample. name: Complete-set, logical-constraint and cross-venue arbitrage
mechanism: Buy a set of outcomes that must pay $1 for less than $1 (both sides of a binary, all outcomes of a multi-outcome event, or logically nested markets in one game), or buy opposite sides of the same question on Polymarket and Kalshi.
time_gap: none (pure price inconsistency); windows reported as 1-3 seconds when they exist
claimed_results: Anton: about 20,000 live order-book pulls over 18 rounds; about 5% of constraints looked violated on mid prices and none on real asks: 'Executable profit: exactly zero.' Leo: binary arbitrage windows last 1-3 seconds; token mint arbitrage -97%; an address claiming $38K from split arbitrage was down $611 on the leaderboard. pm.wiki snippet: on one worked example the Kalshi leg's fee alone was $164.50 against about $50 of gross edge. The promotional post's example of buying Yes and No at 0.48 each cannot occur on a mirrored book.

His book-order warning is confirmed on a live book: asks come 0.99 ... 0.55 and bids 0.01 ... 0.47, so the best price on each side is the last element. The 0.48 + 0.48 example is in the promotional post, which ends with a Telegram contact. The pm.wiki page loaded with 2,855 characters of text and no '$164.50', so that figure is not confirmed. name: Copying profitable wallets
mechanism: Follow large taker orders or a filtered list of historically profitable addresses and enter the same side.
time_gap: none in the follower's favour: the follower trades after the leader has moved the price
claimed_results: Leo, five iterations: following orders over $1,000 won 42.9%; third-party win rates are wrong (one address shown at 83.5% was 50.9% on the official API); many 'whales' are market makers holding both sides; live +$770 against shadow -$148. Hiberius: bought nine times, never sold, wallet banned.
evidence: Leo's 42.9% and '+$770 / -$148' and the guide's 'structurally unprofitable' sentence re-read and correct; Hiberius's ban is in the README. The wallet checks of this pass add two concrete ways a follower list goes stale: the leader moves wallets (swisstony has no volume since September while the same operator trades $80-125M a month as Flaznorp) or changes category (ColdMath, followed as a weather bot, has traded almost only soccer since September and lost 30K there in October). The accounts named in tweet-market stories (sb911, Annica) stopped in August.
requirements: Wallet-tracking feed; nothing else.
fee_sensitivity: Follower pays the taker fee and a worse price than the leader on every trade.
testability: For a leaderboard snapshot taken at date T, compute the same wallets' economic PnL after T with wallet_check monthly data.
red_flags: The product category with the most paid tools and the least evidence.
verification: CONFIRMED. The three sources say what is quoted, and the wallet data of this pass supports the negative conclusion.
